decision: Four human-approved Puck acknowledgment clips are integrated, tested and qualitatively confirmed in Chrome against a local fake robot. No quantitative latency improvement or physical robot validation is claimed.
behavior: Normal conversation and all robot tools remain in the same mode. Quick Puck acknowledgments default on; changing the comparison checkbox requires reconnecting.

Only the exact Gemini3.1 Flash Live model, Puck voice and conversation mode can use the four approved clips. Connect-time preload has a2.5-second bound, byte/hash checks and cancellation; failure uses the existing native response path.

A current accepted server reply must authorize the exact cue. Queue statements require the typed queued marker; Stop says only "Stop requested." No action waits for asset fetching, and duplicate later model acknowledgment is suppressed.
A new successful push-to-talk hold invalidates older output and pending feedback without cancelling robot actions.
Count/unit validation rejects declared unsupported quantities. Voice push-up requests remain enabled; the blanket transcript-based rejection prototype was not integrated.
limitations: The user perceived quicker, consistent acknowledgment in one bounded fake-browser check; no timing in milliseconds was measured.
Manual direct Stop is still visible-only. Dynamic status, failures and the fourth-handshake joke are not cached.

A typed quantity failure carrying command_epoch_required still pauses model motion until reconnect; Stop and status remain available. The refusal can be visible-only when its native audio permit is invalidated.
The required count/unit contract rejects explicit unsupported values but cannot prove the model preserved the spoken request. The six-request actual Google fake-runtime probe is separately preserved.
SDK input transcription is not bound to individual tool calls. The isolated fail-closed guard rejected every voice push-up and was not promoted.
This build does not include the subsequent isolated refusal-audio candidate.
No claim that faster acknowledgment makes motion safer, confirms completion, or removes the need for direct Stop.
human_approval: approved-audio-origin/human-approval.json pins exact4clips andcombinedlisteningWAV. Originalpendingmanifest and actualGoogle generation preserved.
root_operations: Root operated the actual Chrome microphone check against the explicit local fake backend. No physical actuation occurred in that check. This preservation action performed no browser, Google or hardware calls.
purpose: Reduce avoidable post-server-reply acknowledgment delay while preserving the selected Gemini voice; not a speech-recognition change.

browser_observation.source: Root agent reports user-observed test in the current chat; this agent did not operate Chrome or record microphone output.

environment.backend: explicit local fake API on localhost:8000

browser_observation.root_report: User answered "yes and yes" when asked whether the movement confirmation was quicker and consistent in voice, and whether ten push-ups was clearly refused rather than queued.
limits: No instrumented end-to-end or acoustic latency measurement in this observation.
No new raw Google transcript, tool-call trace or microphone recording is attached to this human observation.
The cache reduces the extra acknowledgment-generation wait after a qualifying server reply; it does not improve ASR or initial model tool-planning latency.
This test does not establish physical movement, all four cached phrases in an end-to-end session, general interpretation reliability or every interruption race.
